correctness.rationale: The source establishes geometric smoothness for each nonexceptional parameter. Characteristic-three coefficient comparison gives exact necessary-and-sufficient line-square identities and exact contact discriminants. Exhaustion of all 91 and 6,643 projective rational lines at q=9,81 for every one of the six parameters yields 28 geometric lines over q81, guaranteeing completeness by the classical theta count; four are hyperflex and the remaining 24 have two unique contacts, yielding the stated cycle partitions and zeta functions. The package verifier computes and checks all these facts with exact polynomial finite fields.

evidence: Borges–Korchmáros–Speziali treat the full invariant pencil and identify smoothness and four conic-tangent hyperflex lines, not all 52 contact Frobenius cycles.
Auer–Top isogeny to three elliptic curves controls curve point counts and zeta, not the rational contact fields.
Bethea–Brazelton determine group actions on 28 lines over complex numbers, not arithmetic Frobenius on contact supports.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader classification of curve isogeny factors, geometric line orbits or pencil smoothness is not a stronger theorem about the reduced support of 52 bitangent contact points. No implication from those results to the exact 1/2/4 arithmetic cycle partition was found in the relevant text.

evidence: The published all-odd-field bitangent splitting theorem explicitly says it gives no formula for rational tangency points.
Janasz–Pokora–Zieliński analyze incidence of geometric lines and their intersections, not arithmetic of tangency supports over F9.
Both a=0 and a=1 yield four F9 bitangent lines but different 52-contact Frobenius partitions, distinguishing the claim from existing bitangent-line arithmetic.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new statement cannot be derived from the published numerical line counts, 28-line splitting field, curve zeta or complex S4 orbit sizes without an additional contact-discriminant calculation. The new exact finite computation supplies that information. The common four known hyperflexes are credited and are not alone asserted as novel.

originality.rationale: Geometric pencil smoothness and its four hyperflexes, Auer–Top isogeny data, 4/16/28 rational bitangent-line counts, and complex S4 bitangent orbit sizes are covered prior work and explicitly excluded from novelty. Relevant full primary text and published numerical results do not give the 52-contact Frobenius partitions. The field degree-four contact cycle distinction strictly refines the published quadratic line splitting; an unindexed equivalent remains a genuine historical risk.
residual_risks: Potential equivalent classical contact-coordinate computation for octahedral or Ciani plane quartics not indexed by the searched sources.
Only accessible prior ledgers and targeted published records can be compared, not a global uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The contact support of all geometric odd theta tangencies is an intrinsic natural finite scheme. Exactly classifying its arithmetic Frobenius action on all six non-Hermitian smooth parameters over the first quadratic extension yields a substantive arithmetic splitting boundary: contact degrees four appear even though every bitangent line splits over degree two. This is not implied by the field of the lines or by the common Jacobian zeta and is useful in studying tangential descent and rational exceptional configurations.
